newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL SHARES CLOSE HIGHER ON TECHNICAL BOUNCE.
newsitem.headline: KL SHARES CLOSE HIGHER ON TECHNICAL BOUNCE.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip shares closed higher on Wedneday on a technical rebound after two days of sharp falls, dealers and analysts said.
The benchmark Composite Index closed 1.29 percent, or 11.58 points, higher at 908.83. It had peaked at 919.58.
"It is very much a technical rebound," said a senior foreign fund manager in Kaula Lumpur.

Dealers and analysts said local and foreign institutional investors had been seen selectively buying large-capitalised issues such as Telekom and Maybank. the stocks gaines 10 cents and 50 cents respectively.
Analysts said the rebound was mainly due to local and foreign insitutions selectively bargain hunting for cheapened blue-chip issues.
Debutante Ocean Capital closed at 5.80 ringgit, against a 3.00 ringgit offer price.
Market volume stood at 281 million shares, valued at 1,554 million ringgit. Gainers outpaced losers 433 to 212.
Uncertainty over the direction of the ringgit helped keep buying interest limited, said analysts.
Seemingly conflicting statements by senior ministers on key policy issues was also deterring foreign investors, they said.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot August contract gained 6.6 points to 906.8 with 1,587 lots traded. September futures gained 3.5 points to 908.0 with two lots having changed hands.
